To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GM and non-GGM imports have very high global warming potentials and freshwater ecotoxicities.
GM soy is environmentally better than non-GM soy for the Swedish animal feed market.
GM and non-GMO soy have different environmental impacts, but the difference is not large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
environmental effects of the global soy supply chain.
the environmental consequences of a policy shift from GM to non GM soy in Sweden.
the question of how the environmental impacts of soy imports to Sweden are affected when there is a policy shift towards only non-GM soy feed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the environmental impacts of soy imports to Sweden are higher when GM soy is used as feed.
there are no environmental gains from importing GM soy over non-GM soy in Europe.
the environmental effects of GM and non-GMO soy are comparable and that the environmental effects are highly dependent on the specific feed production and consumption scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no environmental benefits from segregating GM and non-Gm soy in the supply chain.
GM soy has lower impacts in most impact categories when the soy is produced and consumed in Latin America, while non-GM soy has higher impacts when imported to European Union.
GM soy imports have higher negative environmental impacts than non-GM soy imports.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to consider the market effects in order to assess the true environmental impacts.
environmental impacts of soy feed supply lines should not be generalized.
the choice of feed is important for the animal farmer and can have a significant impact on the environment.
